value-guy.invalidation: Flip from a flat book to a fade only if a later freeze dates a convergence clock: a named policy meeting that re-anchors the path, a terms-of-trade break that re-prices a named pair, or a documented term-premium peak followed by a US 10Y lower high. A further rise in US 10s is not invalidation of staying flat.
value-guy.thesis: US 10-year yields are the highest since 2002 and remain a genuine historical dislocation versus the post-2002 distribution, but a one-year percentile is a discovery flag rather than a mean-reversion thesis. The freeze still supplies no dated terms-of-trade, external-balance, productivity, or policy-path clock that says convergence begins on this review; the further cheapening from the prior 5.26 print argues the other way. Canada and Australia 10s and cheap EUR and NZD versus USD are peer dislocations without that clock either, so the book stays flat.

vol-convexity.invalidation: A later freeze supplies a two-way listed options chain with strikes and implied vols on a relevant rates, FX, or equity tenor, or a markable vol or hedge leg appears.
vol-convexity.thesis: US 10Y 5.29 is the highest since 2002, EURUSD 1.1355 is a 17-month low, USDJPY is 156.997, USDCAD is 1.4183, Brent is 103.53, gold is 4186.70, the S&P is 7651.54, and VIX is 16.04, but there is still no listed two-way options chain, strikes, or implied vols beyond that VIX print. Timing on the rates and FX event is uncertain, so linear spot and cash rates are the wrong expression versus bounded-risk convexity. Book stays flat; no invented vol, strike, or premium.
